title: Make Launch compact gates actionable
summary: Made the Launch compact gate strip actionable: each gate now opens the owning page/tab evidence and highlights the concrete row or control. Reduced false compact-gate severity by limiting Settings to settings-owned rows and treating schedule/window advisories as review instead of hard blocked. Restored the missing Audit Launch tab/panel pairing.
reason: Operators saw compact Launch tiles labeled warning/blocked without a direct path to the underlying issue. The strip needed to either point at actionable backend evidence or avoid escalating duplicate/advisory state.
behavior_before: Compact Launch gates only changed the detail text. Settings inherited unrelated launch/schedule/queue rows and could show blocked counts that were not settings problems. Schedule/window duplicate advisories could appear as hard blocked. Audit tab state was inconsistent because the tab/panel pairing was missing in the current partial.
behavior_after: Compact Launch gate clicks navigate to Launch/Queue owner evidence, select and highlight the first concrete issue where available, and reveal hidden evidence transiently without changing persisted UI preferences. Settings compact status is based on settings-owned rows plus policy rows, schedule advisory state is review-level, and the Audit tab/panel pairing is restored.
rollback_plan: Revert the Launch compact gate navigation changes in launchView.scope.js and launchView.js, remove the transient reveal CSS, restore the prior page-launch.html tab markup if needed, and revert the targeted static/browser smoke assertions.
notes: No media policy, FFmpeg, subtitle, audio, pending-publish, source movement, or backend mutation behavior changed.
